Here's what happened on Nov 12 (08:47–12:27 UTC, ~3h40 of stale dashboards):

**What broke:** ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes`, which made ingestion workers run out of memory [1][2]. Sentry caught it: consumer lag >500k messages on the `ingest-events` group, with OOM errors in `ingest/worker/batch.go` [10]. It was declared SEV2 in #incidents with Noa as IC [6].

**Customer data:** none lost. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were just processed late; reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed event counts per workspace match the Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][6].

**Changes being made:**
- Reverting the `max_batch_bytes` default to 1 MB, plus a guard refusing batches over 25% of the container memory limit (bulk import keeps 10 MB via explicit config) — ingest#419 [7]
- A new alert when processing falls more than 5 minutes behind — the rule is in and routed to on-call (KES-431), though the threshold still fires during nightly backfills and is being tuned [2][11]
- Configuration changes now go to a small canary group before full rollout [2]

**Follow-up to be aware of:** Orbitly is claiming an SLA service credit for the incident; Sam is checking the MSA terms with finance [2][8]. Also, Maya asked to push the Postgres 17 cutover off Nov 21 because of this incident and the bank go-live [5].
